On 17 January 1917, The Portuguese Expeditionary Corps (Corpo Expedicionário Português or CEP) was officially established, taking its orders from British military HQ.

Mimo nazwy CEP był na początku zorganizowany jak jedna wzmocniona dywizja piechoty. Taką strukturę zatwierdzono w Lizbonie 17 stycznia. Dowodził nim generał Fernando Tamagnini de Abreu e Silva, wcześniej dowódca dywizji szkolonej na poligonie w Tancos. Już we Francji, w lutym, z inicjatywy brytyjskiej misji wojskowej przy portugalskim dowództwie, dywizję postanowiono przekształcić w korpus złożony z dwóch dywizji, zbudowanych tak jak dywizje brytyjskie.

On 6 April, the 1st Division was pulled back, with the British 55th (West Lancashire) Division extending its lines southwards to fill part of the gap and the 2nd Division taking up the remaining section of the line, now under the operational control of the XI British Corps. The 2nd Division itself, now holding twice the normal divisional frontage, was scheduled to withdraw on 9 April and to be replaced by two British divisions.

Here occurred the famous episode of the 15th Portuguese Battalion's soldier Aníbal Milhais (nickname "Soldier Millions") who, armed only with a Lewis gun, single-handedly defeated two German assaults by laying down intense fire

paragraphs.start: Straty tego dnia są sporne. Starsze portugalskie

quotes.quote: Najbardziej sporne są liczby portugalskie. Starsze portugalskie zestawienia mówiły o ponad tysiącu zabitych i łącznie kilkunastu tysiącach zabitych, rannych, zaginionych i jeńców. Nowsze badania podają około 300–400 zabitych i około 6 tysięcy jeńców, a straty łącznie szacuje się zwykle na około 7–7,5 tysiąca ludzi

In September 1918, already under the command of General Garcia Rosado, the remnants of the CEP started to be re-organised in order to re-enter combat.

By the end of October, four battalions were already combat-capable. These four infantry battalions (I, IV, VIII and IX battalions), together with several artillery, engineer, heavy machine gun and other remaining CEP units, participated in the Hundred Days Offensive.

On 11 November 1918, under the command of Captain Barros Bastos, the 4th Company of the IV Infantry Battalion (former 23rd Battalion of the 1st Division) made the last assault against the Germans on the passage of the Scheldt river, Belgium.

paragraphs.start: Po rozejmie Portugalia nie miała nawet statków

quotes.quote: Portugalia nie miała nawet statków, by sprowadzić z Francji swoich żołnierzy.

On 1 December 1918, a final military parade was held at the Trézennes aerodrome near Aire, from where the first train carrying four hundred Portuguese soldiers left for Cherbourg. On 18 January 1919, a Portuguese delegation took part in the Versailles Peace Conference, and on the following 14 July, a contingent of four hundred men from the CEP took their legitimate place in the victory parade in Paris. Legitimate, but what a sacrifice: 2,160 dead, 5,224 wounded, and 6,678 prisoners.
começou-se a realizar o repatriamento dos efetivos portugueses destacados para o cenário de guerra, contemplando também os prisioneiros que haviam sido retidos nos campos prisionais alemães.
By the Armistice in 1918, the CEP had lost 2,160 dead, 5,224 wounded and 6,678 taken prisoner – 14,000 casualties and losses out of an establishment of 60,000.
